answer: No. A 1 second trigger plus a 1 second run gives a p50 near 1.5 seconds, which passes, but a p99 near 2.5 seconds, which exceeds the 2 second SLA. Micro-batch fails on the tail latency. Its latency floor is the trigger plus the run, so it cannot reliably meet a 2 second SLA. A record-at-a-time engine, with a 10 to 100 ms processing-path floor, is the choice that meets the SLA, even though the team would have to learn a second runtime.
